free_tier.stated: 100,000 API requests a month (each geocoding call, and each query inside a batch call, counts as one request; map tiles count from the same pool), 1,000 search sessions and 5,000 map sessions a month through the SDK, 5 GB of storage in one file; no credit card
free_tier.notes: at either monthly limit the Free plan's maps are suspended for the rest of the month; the Free plan has no paid extra usage. The next plan, Flex, is USD 30 a month for 500,000 API requests and 3,000 search sessions, then USD 0.15 per 1,000 requests.

per_object_cap.stated: a batch geocoding call takes at most 50 semicolon-separated queries, each counted as one request

egress.terms: not applicable: a query API metered in requests and sessions, not bytes

interface_detail: HTTPS GET to api.maptiler.com/geocoding/{query}.json (forward, reverse by longitude,latitude, by feature id, and batch with semicolon-separated queries) with the key in the key parameter; an EU-based endpoint is offered; a request without a key answers HTTP 403 Missing key
tooling: any HTTP client; the MapTiler Client JS library (geocoding.batch) and the MapTiler SDK JS geocoding control, which is metered in sessions rather than requests
chaining: 100,000 storable geocodes a month with no card, shared with map tile requests, so a stored table of up to that many addresses a month can be built through batch calls of 50; past the limit the Free plan stops for the rest of the month, and more is Flex at USD 30 a month or the Geoapify free plan (data-apis/geoapify). Bulk path: the batch endpoint only; no hosted geocoding data download. The last resort is self-hosted: the On-prem Free tile download (OpenStreetMap vectors of 2020) that the user installs and runs with MapTiler Server, tiles only, with no geocoder

evidence.quote: When you hit either of these two limits, you get charged extra (on a paid plan) or your maps get suspended for the rest of the month (on a free plan).

evidence.proved: each query inside a batch call counts as one request
evidence.quote: For example, a batch of 20 queries counts as 20 requests, even though it’s technically one API call.

evidence.proved: a geocoding session covers all search-box interactions in one sitting
evidence.quote: Similarly, in case of [geocoding](https://docs.maptiler.com/guides/developer/location-services/geocoding-search/), a session includes all interactions with a search field in one sitting.

evidence.proved: a batch call takes at most 50 queries
evidence.quote: Each query may be forward, reverse or by feature ID. Maximum of 50 queries are supported.

evidence.proved: every geocoding call needs a MapTiler API key
evidence.quote: You need a MapTiler API key to use this service.

evidence.proved: batch geocoding uses the standard endpoint with semicolon-separated queries
evidence.quote: Just make sure you use semicolons `;` to separate individual requests when sending multiple requests at once.

evidence.proved: each HTTPS geocoding call counts as one request against the plan
evidence.quote: The geocoding API is part of Cloud. You need to have a [free or paid plan](https://www.maptiler.com/cloud/pricing/); each HTTPS API call is counted as an individual request.
